lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Beyond the firelight, the river keeps talking. No one has quite found the courage to sleep.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Skarrow counts mouths. Varrow counts sacks. I used to think a guard only had to count spears.

options.label: Talk about what Varrow owes the town.
Talk about what Maud said of the warmth.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Coll had a little girl. Skarrow has a whole hill of them. Don't ask me to make that come out even. Just... don't let me forget either side.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A log settles. Someone passes the pot without being asked.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: He keeps saying we must trust him. A captain who has to say that has usually stopped listening.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The fire gives everyone the same small share of warmth. For once, nobody has locked it away.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Maud's words return with the smell of woodsmoke: warmth was lent, not given. You look into the coals a little differently.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Then we'd better learn how to give something back.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The smell of scorched timber hangs over the river. Nobody mentions the bridge, but nobody looks away from it either.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: I held that crossing with Coll and Annet. Now Skarrow's people will count their dead on the same planks. It had to be done. Doesn't mean I have to like the taste of it.

options.label: We did what the town hired us to do.
There was no good ending once the spears came out.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Aye. The carts will roll again, and Emberwick eats this winter. Just don't let me call it glory.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The watch shifts in silence. The embers glow steady and hard in the dark.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Aye. Two sides starved of warmth, tearing at each other for scraps. May the Hearth forgive us.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A sudden gust scatters sparks over the river stones. The night turns colder.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Across the shallows, the goblin cookfires twinkle like fallen stars. For the first time in memory, neither side is reaching for their bow.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Halden will spit when he sees the grain tallies. But Mother Skarrow took my hand. Her palms were like dry bark, but she took it.

options.label: Peace bought with bread lasts longer than peace bought with blood.
Keep one eye on the hills. Vorga's hotheads haven't laid down their blades.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: I hope you're right. If Halden tries to cheat them, he answers to my Watch first.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A warm draught drifts from the embers. Somewhere in the dark, a goblin flute plays two slow notes.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: I will. A truce is like thin ice on the millpond. Step carefully or you're under.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The party checks their boots and bows before sleeping. The night remains quiet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Maud's kettle still whistles in the memory. 'It was thrown,' she said, and her blind eyes saw more than anyone in town.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: A hundred years. She sat by that burned bank while three generations grew up, lied to themselves, and died. Is the whole Vale built on borrowed fire?

options.label: If it was thrown, someone threw it. We find out who.
Borrowed or not, people live by it. We keep it burning.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: The Stranger knows. I see how he watches the road east. When the time comes, we make him talk.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A coal cracks open with a soft pop, revealing a red heart of heat.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Aye. The cold doesn't care who threw the stone. It only cares who freezes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The party draws their cloaks closer around the fire. Warmth is precious here.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The stench of ancient ash and bear fur clings to clothes and hair. Ashmaw is gone, but the Hollow feels emptier than before.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: That beast wasn't cruel. Just starving, cold, and driven from its deep den by the chill creeping into the rock. Even the monsters are freezing.

options.label: It died defending the last warm stone in the cave.
The boy is safe with Maud. That is what counts tonight.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: Aye. When the Hearth fails, the strong eat the weak, and everyone starves in the end. We have to rekindle it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The flames flicker low, casting long shadows against the campsite.

lines.speaker: dagna_holt
lines.text: You're right. One life pulled out of the dark. We take our victories where we can find them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Silence settles over the camp. For once, the night feels earned.
